title: Unified Inventory API Integration
business: E-commerce retailers managing fragmented inventory data across multiple legacy warehouse systems.
problem: High latency and maintenance overhead caused by managing disparate API endpoints and inconsistent data formats for real-time stock lookups.
solution: Utilizing Nitro's filesystem routing and built-in storage layer to create a unified, server-side abstraction layer that aggregates inventory data into a single, performant endpoint.
steps: Define a new server route in the server/api directory to act as the inventory aggregator.
Implement the logic to fetch data from legacy warehouse systems using server-side utilities.
Configure the built-in storage layer to cache aggregated results, reducing redundant external API calls.
Expose the unified endpoint to the frontend, ensuring consistent data structures for the client.
outcome: A simplified frontend architecture that interacts with a single, reliable API, resulting in faster page loads and reduced load on legacy backend systems.
limitation: The abstraction layer creates a single point of failure; if the aggregator logic fails, all inventory lookups are blocked. This can be checked by monitoring the server-side error logs and implementing custom error handlers.
